w10_P4_001825: A port authority's fleet figure is 11 times a terminal's figure, and each terminal's figure is 9 times the force taken by one gantry. A gantry carries 4 identical hoists pulling together, so its force is 4 times a single hoist's force in kilonewtons. One hoist drives a block of mass 177000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to the total its drive meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 4 times t. The port's main quay is 400 m long. What is the port authority's fleet figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001841: A quarry conveyor is loaded in stages numbered 1 through 8, and the operator adds together all of those stage numbers from 1 to 8 to get a base figure. The drive then sets the acceleration, in metres per second squared, to that base figure plus 9. The driven mass is 133000 g, and the conveyor belt itself is 60 m long. Ten identical drives share one gantry, three gantries make up a bank, and the quarry runs 3 identical banks. What total force do the quarry's drives supply, in N?
w10_P4_001842: A test track fires a sled whose speed, in metres per second, is 7 times the sum of the two throttle-stage settings, which read 2 and 9. The sled has a mass of 53 kg, and the track's marshalling light is rated at 75 W. The run sheet takes the sled's kinetic energy and adds 25 J for the release actuator. Expressed in kilojoules, the site's daily total then adds 11 kJ for the workshop supply and subtracts 30 kJ credited back by the regenerative brake. What is the site's daily total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001844: A workshop's log entry is 11 times a net energy figure, with 26 J then added for the controller's standby draw. The net figure is the trolley's kinetic energy less 6 J absorbed by the buffer. The trolley has a mass of 8 kg. Its speed in metres per second is 1 less than a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 4 times x, plus 3, equals exactly 0. What is the workshop's log entry, in J?
w10_P4_001845: A velodrome's test rig releases a dummy of mass 18 kg along the banking. The dummy's speed, in metres per second, is 7 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 20, equals exactly 0. The rig runs two identical lanes at once, so a session's total, in kilojoules, is twice the energy of one dummy. The session report then subtracts 6 kJ credited back by the regenerative catcher. What does the session report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_001850: A luge training centre launches a sled of mass 48 kg. Its launch speed, in metres per second, is 6 more than a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 14 times x, plus 48, equals exactly 0. The centre runs 7 launches in a heat and 9 heats in a day. The centre's start-gate lamp draws 55 W. The daily log then subtracts 3 J recovered by the catch net. What does the daily log record, in J?
w10_P4_001851: A haulage depot's yearly figure is 3 times its quarterly figure, and the quarterly figure is 6 times a shift's figure. A shift covers 9 identical trolley runs, so its figure is 9 times the energy of a single run. A trolley has a mass of 47 kg, and the depot's inspection lamp draws 80 W. A trolley's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 7 times the value, plus 12, comes to exactly 0. What is the depot's yearly figure, in J?
w10_P4_001857: A lift-testing hall reports the force taken by its 7 identical guide frames together. For one frame the reported force is the force driving the test car plus 30 N for the guide-shoe friction. The car has a mass of 115 kg, and the hall's shaft is 24 m deep. The car's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. What force does the hall report for all 7 frames together, in kN?
w10_P4_001868: A laboratory receives 301 washers of one size and 190 of another, and it groups them into identical trays using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. A bench cart of mass 24000 g then rolls at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that tray size. The bench's energy sheet takes the cart's kinetic energy and adds 21 J drawn by the timer. It then subtracts 13 J recovered at the stop, and a further 26 J credited to the mains supply. What does the sheet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001871: A hangar's summary is 6 times a single bay's balance, because six identical bays operate together. A bay's balance is the force driving its tug, expressed in kilonewtons, less 19 kN allowed for the anchor chain. The tug pushes a load of mass 189 kg. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 93 and 14 exactly. What is the hangar's summary, in kN?
w10_P4_001872: A rail-gun demonstration rig accelerates a slug of mass 16000 g. The slug's exit speed, in metres per second, equals the total that the rig's charge meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second of a shot, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 6 times t. The rig's cooling pump is rated at 300 W. Each shot's booked energy is the slug's kinetic energy less 8 J absorbed by the muzzle brake, and the rig fires 6 shots in a demonstration. How much energy does a full demonstration account for, in kJ?
w10_P4_001882: A ferry terminal tests a trolley of mass 52000 g on the linkspan. The trolley's speed, in metres per second, is 2 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 18, is exactly 0. Two trolleys run on each ramp, two ramps serve each berth, and the terminal operates 11 identical berths. How much energy do all the terminal's trolleys carry at once, in J?
w10_P4_001888: A bakery line receives 40 trays of one type and 117 of another, and it stacks them in identical columns using the largest column height that divides both counts exactly. A test carriage of mass 47000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that column height. The line's log takes the driving force, adds 21 N for the chain drag and then a further 29 N for the guide brushes. The line's oven is rated at 9 kW. Four identical carriages run side by side, and the log reports 4 times the single-carriage figure. What does the log report, in kN?
w10_P4_001896: A wind-farm workshop's report is 3 times a bay total, with 20 J then subtracted for the test lamp. A bay total covers 8 identical drop tests, so it is 8 times a single test's figure, and a single test's figure is the weight's kinetic energy less 5 J absorbed by the arrestor. The dropped weight has a mass of 27 kg. Its impact speed, in metres per second, is 3 times the sum of the two height-gauge readings, which are 3 and 15. What is the workshop's report figure, in J?
w10_P4_001897: A drop-tower rig releases a carrier of mass 24 kg. The carrier's release speed in metres per second is read from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 3 times the cube of the dial setting plus 4 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 3. The tower's guide rail is 30 m long. Expressed in kilojoules, the site's energy sheet takes the carrier's kinetic energy, adds 27 kJ for the winch, adds 17 kJ for the compressor, and adds a further 29 kJ for the site cabin. What does the energy sheet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001900: A mining haulage company's annual figure is 5 times its site figure, and the site figure is the fleet total less 20 kJ credited back by the regenerative brakes. The fleet total is 4 times the energy of one skip, because 4 identical skips run at once. Each skip has a mass of 35 kg on the scale rig used for the estimate, and the rig's headlamp draws 65 W. A skip's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that the rig's meter accumulates between the 3rd and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 4 times t squared plus 6 times t. What is the company's annual figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001910: A textile mill's floor report is 10 times the force taken by one loom frame, expressed in kilonewtons. A frame carries two identical beaters, so it takes twice the corrected force of a single beater. For one beater the corrected force is the driving force plus 20 N for the return-spring preload. That beater drives a mass of 193000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 230 and 73 exactly. The mill's overhead lighting is rated at 400 W. What does the floor report give, in kN?
w10_P4_001914: A materials lab meters its hydraulic pump through a run, and at time t seconds the pump's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 1 times t. The lab takes the total that the meter accumulates between the 1st and the 2nd second, subtracts 8, adds 14, and then adds 7 to obtain the ram's speed in metres per second. The ram carries a striker of mass 54000 g. The lab's extraction fan draws 250 W. How much kinetic energy does the striker carry, in kJ?
w10_P4_001919: A school lab's summary is 11 times a paired-bench figure, expressed in kilojoules. A paired-bench figure is twice a single bench's balance, since the benches are always used in pairs. One bench's balance is the glider's kinetic energy less 29 J drawn by the air blower. The glider has a mass of 3 kg, and the lab's extractor fan draws 45 W. The glider's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. What is the lab's summary, in kJ?
w10_P4_001923: A packaging plant's final tally adds 20 N for the frame's own reaction to 5 times a line total. A line total is 11 times one pusher's corrected force, and a pusher's corrected force is the force on its carton plus 21 N for the belt drag. The carton has a mass of 12 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 3 times the sum of the two ramp settings, which read 8 and 3. What is the plant's final tally, in N?
w10_P4_001924: A steelworks records a weekly figure of 7 times its daily figure, where the daily figure is a shift total plus 10 J for the control room. A shift total is 9 times the energy of one hammer blow. The hammer has a mass of 48000 g, and its position along the guide, in metres, is 5 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 6 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The works uses how fast the hammer is moving at the instant 1 second after release. What is the steelworks' weekly figure, in J?
w10_P4_001926: A foundry's test record ends with twice a single trolley's kinetic energy, less 5 J absorbed by the buffer. The trolley has a mass of 43 kg, and the foundry's inspection lamp draws 70 W. Its speed in metres per second is found by taking a calibration reading and subtracting 7. That calibration reading comes from a chart on which a plotted quantity equals 2 times the cube of the dial setting minus 5 times the square of the dial setting, and the reading is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 2. What does the test record end with, in J?
w10_P4_001938: A brewery's annual figure is 9 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 9 times a weekly figure. A weekly figure covers 3 identical crate runs, so it is 3 times the energy of a single run. A crate has a mass of 41000 g. Its speed along the roller table, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 210 and 178 exactly. What is the brewery's annual figure, in J?
w10_P4_001943: A model-railway test bench launches a wagon of mass 9 kg along a level rail. The launch speed in metres per second is built up in three steps: a number x is multiplied by 10, then 14 is subtracted, and the result is doubled. The number x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 9 times x, plus 18, equals exactly 0. The bench's controller draws 35 W. How much kinetic energy does the wagon carry, in J?
w10_P4_001945: A test house's report gives twice the energy of a single carriage, in kilojoules, because the house runs a mirrored pair of tracks. The carriage has a mass of 43 kg, and the house's ventilation fan draws 90 W. The carriage's speed, in metres per second, is 3 times the total that the track meter accumulates between the 0th and the 1st second of a run. The meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 2 times t. What does the test house's report give, in kJ?
